title: “Why Did You Deceive Me?” The Question We All Ask G-d - Women's Vayetzei Class
blurb: Why the Greatest Decisions of Your Life Are Made Beyond Your Conscious Mind Why did Jacob have to be deceived into marrying Leah? Why couldn't Lavan simply tell him that the older daughter must marry first? Why was deception necessary to bring about the most consequential marriages in Jewish history? In this profoundly moving women's class on Parshas Vayeitzei, Rabbi YY Jacobson explores one of the deepest mysteries of the human soul: The greatest choices of our lives are sometimes the very choices our conscious minds would never make. Jacob loved Rachel, but Leah represented a dimension of spiritual depth that transcended everything he could understand, anticipate, or willingly embrace. Rachel embodied the light he could recognize; Leah embodied an infinite truth that would shatter his expectations and transform his destiny. Sometimes the divine within us chooses a journey that our conscious selves would reject. What feels like the destruction of our plans may become the birthplace of a self we never knew existed. Through a strange Talmudic story about a man who forgot a bundle of grain in the field, the mysterious blessings of Isaac, the courage of Queen Esther, and the hidden origins of Moshiach, we discover why the deepest divine energy sometimes emerges only when our familiar sense of control is suspended. title: Mitteler Rebbe's Padah Beshalom part 4/9 שערי תשובה ד"ה פדה בשלום (פרק ה-ו)
blurb: Link to מאמר PDF Getting into the main topic of the מאמר, the מיטעלער רבי explains the difference between מקיף and פנימי using a משל from the way the נשמה energizes the body. Based on that, the מיטעלער רבי introduces us to two types of מקיף: A מקיף which is connected to פנימי, and a מקיף that remains מקיף. The explanations begins with a משל of two forms of רצון (which is generally מקיף), with this שיעור finishing with the discussion of the first type: A רצון that can be overwhelmed by a stronger רצון, being that it operates within the parameters of כחות פנימיים, which can be changed. the מיטעלער רבי provides a געשמאקע משל of someone who strongly desires money, yet when a life-or-death situation, or even an opportunity for honor and greatness, arises, that new desire overwhelms the first one.
